prompt: Overnight, a room's temperature after $t$ hours is $T = 18 + \frac{6}{t}$ degrees. As $t$ gets larger and larger, what temperature is the room settling toward, in degrees?
hint: Watch the piece $\frac{6}{t}$. What happens to it when $t$ becomes huge?

hints.text: Watch the piece $\frac{6}{t}$. What happens to it when $t$ becomes huge?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Look at $\frac{1}{t}$ alone: at $t = 10$ it is $0.1$, at $t = 100$ it is $0.01$, at $t = 1000$ it is $0.001$. Bigger bottom means a tinier fraction, heading to $0$. Now do the same with $\frac{6}{t}$ and add the $18$ back on.
At $t = 6$, $\frac{6}{t} = 1$; at $t = 60$ it is $0.1$; at $t = 600$ it is $0.01$. It is fading to $0$.

explanation: Split the rule into two pieces: a fixed $18$ and a fading $\frac{6}{t}$.
A fixed top over a growing bottom shrinks toward $0$: $1$, then $0.1$, then $0.01$.
So the whole thing heads to $18 + 0$.
The room settles at $18$ degrees — it gets closer and closer without ever quite landing.

alternativeExplanations.title: A table of the night
steps: Every row is closer to 18 than the one before, and none ever dips below it. The limit is 18.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read it off the graph
steps: Sketch the curve: it starts high and slides down, flattening out as it goes right.
Draw a horizontal line at 18 — the curve hugs it more and more tightly but never crosses.
That line is called an asymptote, and its height is the limit: 18 degrees.
